content.text: {"claims":[{"claim":1,"text":"Semi-supervised anomaly detection methods can be trained on mostly unlabelled data by incorporating labelled anomalies as constraints or by assigning pseudo-labels to unlabelled samples while filtering high-uncertainty predictions to avoid corrupting the minority class in imbalanced industrial streams.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-00960","field":"abstract","quote":"incorporates labelled anomalies as must-outside constraints during kernel optimisation"},{"id":"SYN-PUB-00962","field":"abstract","quote":"Self-training iteratively assigns pseudo-labels to unlabelled samples and retrains a classifier"},{"id":"SYN-PUB-00962","field":"abstract","quote":"only samples whose entropy falls below a calibrated threshold enter the pseudo-labelled pool"}]},{"claim":2,"text":"Anomaly detection models can be optimised to run inference on edge devices with strict memory budgets through quantisation and model selection, with a quantised convolutional network fitting within 200 KB and achieving 97% of its full-precision AUPRC on an ARM board.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-00963","field":"abstract","quote":"Deploying anomaly detection at the network edge requires balancing model accuracy against strict memory budgets"},{"id":"SYN-PUB-00963","field":"abstract","quote":"The quantised convolutional network fits within 200 KB and achieves 97% of its full-precision AUPRC while meeting a 5 ms per-window latency budget on the ARM board"}]}]}
